call.target_note: the callee at 0x55275b0 IS an FDE start (994 bytes, .eh_frame+0x002c9c6c, CIE 0x00000000, the same CIE as the window), but its body is excluded here; only the call encoding and the FDE record are retained, so no claim about what it computes is made

coordinate_system: ELF virtual addresses, no runtime rebase

function.padding_note: two int3 bytes (0xcc) at [0x54e1b7e, 0x54e1b80) pad the window to the next FDE at 0x54e1b80

edges.note: null base pointer fails before any other check and returns 22
null second pointer fails and returns 22 (its pointee is never read)
null third pointer fails and returns 22
stack argument one below the required 8 fails and returns 22
stack argument one above the required 8 fails and returns 22
pointee one below 0x30 fails and returns 22
pointee one above 0x30 fails and returns 22
every gate failing at once still returns exactly 22, not a different code
all five gates pass: the callee is called with base-derived arguments and the window returns 0
a second base shows the callee arguments are derived from the base, not constants

rule.formula: return 22 (0x16) unless rcx != 0 and r8 != 0 and r9 != 0 and the first stack argument == 8 and the qword at [r8] == 0x30; when all five gates pass, call 0x55275b0 with rdi = entry rdi (passthrough), rsi = [r9], rdx = rcx + 8, rcx = rcx + 0x10, r8 = rcx + 0x18, r9 = rcx + 0x20, first stack argument = rcx + 0x28, second stack argument = rcx, and return 0
rule.formula_note: the first stack argument is the seventh argument overall: at entry [rsp] holds the return address and [rsp + 8] holds it; after sub rsp, 8 the window reads it as [rsp + 0x10]. The gate order in bytes is rcx, then r8, then (stack argument, r9) combined by or, then [r8], but the rule is a pure conjunction, so order does not change the result. The failure value is exactly 22 on every failure path (three separate mov eax, 0x16 sites), not a generic error code; the window writes nothing on failure. The pass path returns exactly 0 (xor eax, eax after the call), whatever the callee returns, because the callee result is discarded. The callee body is excluded even though it is an FDE start.
rule.inputs: base pointer (rcx, must be nonzero; all callee pointer arguments derive from it), second pointer (r8, must be nonzero; its pointee must equal 0x30), third pointer (r9, must be nonzero; its pointee becomes the callee rsi), first stack argument (must equal 8 exactly), entry rdi (passed through to the callee untouched)
